content: Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of teniposide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of terbinafine by enhancing hepatic CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin lowers the levels or effects of theophylline by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Rifampin reduces the levels of ticagrelor by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Avoid coadministration of ticagrelor with potent CYP3A inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tobramycin by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin lowers the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Loss of or reduced response to tofacitinib may occur when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels of toremifene by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP3A4 inducers increase the rate of toremifene metabolism, lowering its steady-state serum concentration. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tramadol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducers reduces the AUC of tramadol and its active metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol). Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of vadadustat through mechanisms involving OAT1/OAT3 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor closely for excessive or rapid increases in hemoglobin response and for adverse reactions. Rifampin and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec can potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Consider alternative medications in cases of potential drug interactions. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of valsartan by mechanisms involving hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Caution and monitoring are recommended. In vitro studies suggest valsartan is a substrate of OATP1B1, and coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to valsartan. Vemurafenib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity, while rifampin decreases vemurafenib levels by enhancing P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels of vilazodone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vincristine and vincristine liposomal by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels of vortioxetine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and increasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose when coadministered with a strong CYP inducer for more than 14 days, but do not exceed three times the original dose. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zaleplon by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels of zidovudine by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zonisamide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases the levels of acetaminophen (oral, IV, and rectal) by increasing its metabolism, potentially enhancing the production of hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of aliskiren by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of alosetron by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of alvimopan by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of ampicillin by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Bentonite reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of bisoprolol by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of caffeine by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of celecoxib by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of chloramphenicol by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cimetidine by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diazepam by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of diclofenac by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of enalapril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Ethanol reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fexofenadine by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance is unknown. Fluconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of fluvastatin by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism and increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of fosinopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of frovatriptan by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ibuprofen (oral and IV) by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of imidapril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of isosorbide dinitrate and isosorbide mononitrate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Ketoconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin increases the effects of leflunomide by increasing its metabolism into its active metabolite. The clinical significance is unknown. Levoketoconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of levothyroxine and liothyronine by increasing their metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of lisinopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of loratadine by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of meloxicam by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism and increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Miconazole vaginal reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of modafinil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of moexipril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of morphine by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of nevirapine by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of nortriptyline by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ondansetron by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of opium tincture by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of oxacillin by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of perindopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of pirmenol by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of piroxicam by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Posaconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of quinapril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of ramipril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of riluzole by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of sulfamethoxazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels of tibolone by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is theoretical, and the clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of trandolapril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Voriconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers reduces plasma concentrations of abemaciclib and its metabolites. Close monitoring is required. Rifampin reduces the levels of abiraterone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Avoid coadministration of abiraterone with strong CYP3A4 inducers.
